title: Reproducible Data Pipeline Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Import, transformation, validation, and export workflows with reproducibility checks. The Reproducible Data Pipeline Database makes data processing repeatable: every pipeline is a versioned sequence of stages — import, clean, transform, validate, export — where each stage declares its inputs, code version, parameters, and expected output hash. Re-run the pipeline on the same inputs and you must get the same outputs, or the pipeline fails loudly. 'It worked on my machine' is replaced by pinned environments, content hashes, and validation gates between stages.

title: Reproducible Data Pipeline Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Pipeline anatomy: DAG of stages; each stage = {name, code_ref (versioned), params, inputs[], outputs[], expected_hash}. Content hashing: SHA-256 over canonical serialization; any byte change changes the hash. Validation gates: schema validation (types, required fields), range checks, referential checks, statistical checks (row counts within expected bands). Environment: runtime + library versions pinned; random seeds fixed and recorded. Replay: re-execute from recorded inputs with recorded code/params; compare output hashes. Failure taxonomy: input drift (hash mismatch at import), code drift (unpinned dependency), nondeterminism (unseeded randomness), gate failure (validation rejects).

demo.code: function jw(a,b){a=a.toLowerCase();b=b.toLowerCase();if(a===b)return 1;let m=0;const n=Math.min(a.length,b.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(a[i]===b[i])m++;return m/Math.max(a.length,b.length);}const pairs=[['Jon Smith','John Smith'],['Jon Smith','Maria Garcia']];const scored=pairs.map(([x,y])=>({x,y,s:+jw(x,y).toFixed(2)}));J({scored});assert(scored[0].s>scored[1].s,'match');

title: Reproducible Data Pipeline Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: hash test (identical inputs produce identical hashes); gate test (invalid data fails the gate); replay test (recorded runs reproduce); drift test (tampered stages are identified); determinism test. Limitations: external services need cached responses for replay; wall-clock timestamps must be virtualized; large data needs chunked hashing (documented pattern). Every run record is immutable once written.

demo.title: Execution: pipeline stage hashing and replay
demo.code: const crypto=require('crypto');function h(s){return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex').slice(0,8);}const stages=['import','clean','validate','export'];const data='raw-data-v1';let cur=data;const hashes=stages.map(s=>{cur=s+':'+cur;return s+'='+h(cur);});const replay=(()=>{let c=data;return stages.map(s=>{c=s+':'+c;return s+'='+h(c);});})();J({hashes:hashes.length,replayMatch:JSON.stringify(hashes)===JSON.stringify(replay)});assert(JSON.stringify(hashes)===JSON.stringify(replay),'replay');
